The cheapest courses in Australia for international students in 2027 are generally vocational certificates and diplomas. Among the current published options we checked, TAFE Queensland lists Certificate III in Fitness at A$5,400 total for six months, Certificate III in Individual Support at A$6,300, and Certificate III in Hospitality at A$6,400.

University study costs considerably more. Southern Cross University, for example, has set A$27,000 annual tuition for most eligible international courses in 2027.

So, if you are searching for cheap courses in Australia for international students, VET is usually the first place to look. But the lowest tuition fee is not automatically the best value.

If you are planning to study in Australia, compare the course level, CRICOS status, duration, location, scholarship opportunities and total cost before choosing the smallest number on a fee sheet.

Quick answer: Lower-cost 2027 study options currently start at around A$5,400 for selected VET certificates, around A$15,000 to A$20,000 for several practical diplomas, and around A$27,000 per year at the affordable end of university study.

Here is the important distinction. A short skill set can technically cost less than these qualifications. TAFE Queensland, for example, lists some skill sets at only a few hundred dollars.

That does not make them the answer to this search.

Most international students searching for the cheapest course to study in Australia for international students want a meaningful qualification that fits an actual study plan, not simply the lowest-priced training item in a database.

Cheapest TAFE Courses for International Students

TAFE is one of the first places to look when your budget is tight.

Vocational Education and Training, usually shortened to VET, focuses strongly on practical and employment-related skills. Many qualifications are shorter than university degrees, which can reduce the total tuition bill.

TAFE Queensland's 2027 international price list includes several certificates below A$10,000, including fitness, individual support, hospitality, accounts administration, laboratory skills, health services and information technology.

Some courses also have both January and July starts.

That flexibility matters. Missing the first intake does not necessarily mean waiting another year.

There is another point students sometimes overlook. Australia's qualification system is not just a collection of unrelated course names. The Australian Qualifications Framework, or AQF, is the national policy for regulated Australian qualifications and connects vocational and higher education qualification types within one framework.

You can check the Australian Qualifications Framework if you want to understand how certificate, diploma and degree levels relate to one another.

That is useful when a cheaper VET course forms part of a sensible progression route rather than becoming a dead end.

This is where a cheap headline price can mislead.

A A$16,600 diploma that directly fits your goals may offer better value than a A$6,000 certificate followed by another course you never originally intended to take.

Cheapest Foundation Courses in Australia for International Students

Foundation study is not automatically cheap.

That is slightly counterintuitive because students often assume a foundation programme must cost less than a degree. At major university pathway providers, the opposite can happen.

UNSW College currently publishes these tuition fees for 2027:

These are tuition figures only, and UNSW College states that fees are reviewed annually.

You can compare the current amounts on the UNSW College fees page.

Why would a student choose foundation study when a VET certificate can cost far less?

Because the purpose is different.

A foundation programme can prepare a student who does not meet direct undergraduate entry requirements for progression into university. In that situation, the relevant question is not simply which course is cheapest. It is which pathway gets you into the intended degree without creating unnecessary delays.

If you already meet direct undergraduate requirements, paying for an extra pathway may make little sense.

Students with less straightforward academic histories may also want to check how Australian institutions can assess previous study gaps before choosing a pathway.

Cheapest Bachelor Degree in Australia for International Students

At university level, the word "cheap" becomes relative.

For 2027, Southern Cross University provides one of the clearest affordable benchmarks. Through its Access27 pricing, annual international tuition for most eligible courses is A$27,000.

The university excludes several programmes, including the Master of Nursing, Bachelor of Veterinary Technology, Bachelor of Veterinary Medicine, higher degree research and some non-award programmes.

That means A$27,000 should not be interpreted as the fee for every course.

Still, it is a useful benchmark for students researching the cheapest degree in Australia for international students.

Lower-cost bachelor's options are more commonly found in fields such as business, arts, social sciences, education-related subjects and some computing programmes than in medicine, dentistry, veterinary science or other resource-intensive clinical fields.

If a university degree is your real goal, compare public universities available across Australia rather than choosing an unrelated vocational course purely because its tuition is lower.

This article deliberately focuses on courses and qualification costs. It does not try to turn the page into a full ranking of Australia's cheapest universities, which is a different search intent and deserves separate coverage.

Cheapest Master's Degree in Australia for International Students

Postgraduate students can use the same Southern Cross University pricing as a useful starting benchmark.

Most eligible international courses under Access27 carry annual tuition of A$27,000 in 2027.

But annual tuition alone can give you the wrong answer.

Think about it this way. One master's degree costs A$28,000 per year for two years. Another charges more per year but becomes shorter because you receive relevant credit.

The first has the cheaper annual fee. The second may have the lower total cost.

For master's students, compare:

annual tuition, total duration, available credit, scholarship value and living expenses for the entire programme.

That produces a much more useful comparison than chasing a single "cheapest master's" figure.

Are Nursing Courses Cheap in Australia?

Usually, no.

Nursing can offer strong professional value, but clinical training, placements and professional requirements push costs above many business, hospitality or community-service qualifications.

TAFE Queensland lists the Diploma of Nursing at A$33,600 for relevant 2027 intakes, with CRICOS code 109308H and a duration of around 18 months.

Compare that with A$6,300 for Certificate III in Individual Support.

The difference is large, but the two qualifications also lead to very different educational and professional outcomes.

That is why tuition should never become the only selection criterion.

Scholarships Can Make a More Expensive Course Cheaper

Affordable courses in Australia for international students are not always the programmes with the lowest advertised tuition.

Scholarships can change the calculation.

For students commencing in 2027, UniSQ has published an International Student Support Scholarship worth a 10% tuition fee reduction for eligible students.

Its International Excellence Scholarship offers a 15% reduction in tuition fees for eligible high-achieving international students starting in 2027.

For example, a 15% scholarship on A$30,000 of tuition reduces the bill by:

A$4,500

That is enough to change which university represents better value.

You can review the 2027 UniSQ International Student Support Scholarship and International Excellence Scholarship for the current eligibility details.

You can also compare other Australian scholarship opportunities before accepting an offer.

Do not deduct a scholarship from your final budget until the university has confirmed that you qualify.

Tuition Is Not Your Total Cost

This is where many cheap-course comparisons fall apart.

Suppose you choose a one-year Diploma of Community Services with tuition of A$16,600.

The Australian Government's current financial capacity requirement uses A$29,710 for an individual student's living costs, although your actual expenses can be higher depending on where and how you live.

A simple planning calculation therefore begins like this:

The Department of Home Affairs and Study Australia make clear that students also need to consider tuition, travel and other expenses when demonstrating financial capacity.

That means a A$16,600 course does not mean you need only A$16,600 to study in Australia.

You still need to consider:

A small tuition saving can disappear quickly if your accommodation is substantially more expensive.

If two providers charge similar fees, compare Australian cities and their living conditions before deciding which option is genuinely cheaper.

Do International Students Need Health Cover?

Yes.

OSHC costs differ according to the insurer, length of cover and whether you need single, couple or family insurance.

That makes a single national "average price" less helpful than an actual quotation for your circumstances.

Before comparing final offers, check how health insurance works for international students in Australia and include the relevant policy cost in your budget.

Can Regional Study Reduce the Cost?

Often, yes. But not automatically.

A regional campus may have cheaper accommodation than an expensive central location in Sydney or Melbourne. Tuition, however, can remain the same across several campuses.

So this shortcut does not always work:

regional course = cheaper course

Instead, calculate the complete package:

tuition + rent + transport + course duration + scholarship + compulsory costs.

A course with slightly higher tuition can still work out cheaper if the student's everyday living expenses are lower.

Students considering employment and longer-term migration outcomes can also explore courses linked with post-study residency planning, but do not select a qualification because somebody promises permanent residence.

No Australian course guarantees PR.

How to Check Whether a Cheap Course Is Genuine

Use official Australian Government sources before paying a deposit.

You can search the official Australian Government CRICOS register directly.

For every low-cost course you shortlist:

  1. Confirm the provider and course on CRICOS.
  2. Match the CRICOS code with the provider's own course information.
  3. Check the international tuition for your actual intake year.
  4. Confirm the duration, campus and entry requirements.
  5. Identify whether the qualification sits within the AQF where relevant.
  6. Calculate the total programme cost, not only the first instalment.

A small difference in course names can matter.

Check the code, not just the headline.

Can International Students Work While Studying?

Part-time work can help with everyday expenses.

It should not become the foundation of your tuition plan.

Job availability, hours and earnings can change. Your course fees do not disappear when work becomes difficult to find.

Which Cheap Course Should You Choose?

Start with the outcome you need.

If your priority is the lowest practical tuition, investigate eligible VET certificates first.

If you need a stronger vocational qualification, compare diplomas.

If you do not meet direct undergraduate entry requirements, check whether a foundation programme genuinely solves that problem.

If your intended career requires a bachelor's or master's degree, compare affordable universities, scholarships and course duration rather than switching to an unrelated course simply because it costs less.

The AQF can also help you understand the difference between qualification types and pathways before you compare prices.

And if you are still comparing the wider destination rather than one qualification, our guidance on studying in Australia as an international student can help you consider entry requirements, costs and study planning together.

Frequently Asked Questions

What are the cheapest courses in Australia for international students in 2027?

Some of the cheapest current 2027 options are VET certificates. TAFE Queensland lists Certificate III in Fitness at A$5,400, Certificate III in Individual Support at A$6,300, Certificate III in Hospitality at A$6,400, and Certificate III in Accounts Administration at A$6,600.

What is the cheapest course in Australia for international students?

Among the practical qualifications reviewed here, Certificate III in Fitness at TAFE Queensland is one of the lowest-priced 2027 options at A$5,400 total for six months. Its CRICOS code is 109306K.

What is the cheapest TAFE course for international students?

Certificate III in Fitness is currently one of TAFE Queensland's cheapest published international qualifications for 2027 at A$5,400 total. Other low-cost Certificate III programmes begin from around A$6,300.

What are the cheapest diploma courses in Australia for international students?

Current lower-cost examples include the Diploma of Community Services and Diploma of Mental Health at A$16,600 each, while a Business and Leadership and Management diploma package is listed at A$17,800.

What are the cheapest foundation courses in Australia for international students?

Foundation study generally costs more than entry-level VET. UNSW College lists its 2027 Transition Program at A$29,980, Standard Foundation Program at A$43,650, and Standard Plus Foundation Program at A$48,750.

What is the cheapest degree in Australia for international students?

There is no permanent single cheapest degree because fees differ by institution and course. As a useful 2027 benchmark, Southern Cross University has set annual international tuition at A$27,000 for most eligible courses, with several exclusions.

What is an affordable master's degree in Australia for international students?

Southern Cross University's Access27 pricing sets most eligible international courses at A$27,000 per year in 2027. Students should still compare total duration, credit and scholarships before deciding which master's is cheapest overall.

Are there scholarships for international students in Australia in 2027?

Yes. UniSQ has published a 10% International Student Support Scholarship and a 15% International Excellence Scholarship for eligible students commencing in 2027.

Can I choose a cheap course for PR in Australia?

You can consider career prospects and migration pathways when selecting a qualification, but no course guarantees permanent residence. If this matters to your long-term plan, review post-study permanent residency pathways separately.

How can I verify that a cheap Australian course is legitimate?

Search the official Australian Government CRICOS register, check the provider's published international fee, match the CRICOS code, confirm your intake and review the qualification level before paying a deposit.

Choose the Cheapest Suitable Course, Not Just the Cheapest Number

The cheapest courses in Australia for international students currently start at around A$5,400 for selected 2027 VET qualifications, while several practical diplomas sit in the mid-A$10,000 range. At university level, A$27,000 per year provides a useful current benchmark for many eligible lower-fee courses.

But a cheap course becomes expensive if you have to change programmes, extend your studies or start again.

Choose the lowest-cost qualification that still fits your academic background, career direction and financial plan.

Check its CRICOS status. Understand its AQF level where relevant. Confirm the latest fee and intake. Calculate living expenses. Then look at genuine scholarships before accepting an offer.

That is a much better definition of affordable study.
